//rawDir: Where scripts/screenshots.mjs writes its captures and, next to each, <capture>.marks.json; {locale} is replaced per language.
//locales: Each locale needs a config/copy.<locale>.json and a capture folder. `dir` there drives RTL.
//style: For the whole set. sublines: show each slide's subline under its headline (off: a thumbnail has room for one message; a slide can still ask for its own with "subline": true). maxLines: a headline that needs more lines than this is stepped down in size until it fits.
//slides: Order is the store order. raw: a capture in rawDir. layout: where the copy is — top (the phone runs off the bottom edge) or bottom (it runs off the top). Alternate them. background: a preset in theme.json. device: iphone | pixel. phone: { width (percent of the canvas height, 39 by default), tilt (degrees), nudge [x, y] (x in App Store canvas widths, y in canvas heights) }. second: another capture as a phone behind the first (raw, width, tilt, nudge; "front": true puts it in front). callouts: pieces of the capture lifted out of the phone — see //callouts. The whole model, with the reasons: reference/composition.md.
//callouts: Each lifts one piece of the slide's own capture: { mark, scale, tilt, shift, anchor, pad, radius }. mark: a name from <capture>.marks.json (named in scripts/lib/shots.mjs, written by `npm run screenshots`), so the piece is found in every language and follows the app when a screen changes. scale: how much bigger than in the phone (1.1–1.5). tilt: degrees. shift: [x, y] in screen widths. anchor: the edge that stays put while it grows (center, top, bottom, start, end, top-start …). pad: grow the piece on every side, in capture widths (for a piece that has no card of its own). radius: its corner, in capture widths, when the mark's own is not wanted. A fixed "crop": [x, y, w, h] (fractions of the capture) works too, but is the same spot in every language.

slides.//: The opening slide says what the app is: home (the clean-up card, the tiles, the trips) in front, a trip behind it. No call-out: two phones are enough.
The first two trip cards lifted out: the place names are the promise.

iPhone only (Android makes a folder, not an album): Play's slide list leaves it out. The phone is smaller than usual, so its bottom bar with the button stays on the canvas and the button can be lifted.
The clean-up card with its number: the screen's own words for the headline's promise.
The scan, with its line about staying on the device.

//stickers: Drawings from assets/stickers/, anchored to a slide by id. x: in slide widths from that slide's leading edge to the sticker's centre — 1 is the seam to the next slide, so the sticker shows half on each and the listing reads as one strip. y: in slide heights from the top. size: its width, in App Store canvas widths. rotate: degrees. layer: front (default) or back (behind the phone). Keep them out of the copy: y roughly between 0.3 and 0.7 is clear on both layouts. A target with its own slide list keeps each sticker on its slide; the spill goes to whichever slide comes next there.
//targets: Exact export pixels. App Store Connect requires the "iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display)" slot (iPhone 6.1"/6.3"), which accepts only 1206x2622 or 1179x2556 portrait; the large 6.9"/6.5" slots are optional and scaled from it. So one target, one folder: screenshots/store/iphone-6.3/<locale>/. Google Play is the second target, with its own captures (rawDir).
//ribbon: The corner ribbon with the copy file's `ribbon` word, per target and on the feature graphic: true = every slide, "first" = the first slide only, false or absent = none. The same switch lets a target show the price points of the copy files ({ "text": …, "price": true }). Fotonest has an in-app purchase, so it is off everywhere and the copy files have no ribbon and no price points: "free" on a screenshot of an app that sells something is misleading on Play and rejected by Apple (guideline 2.3.7). See reference/store-specs.md.

targets.//: Google Play phone screenshots, from the Android captures (`npm run screenshots -- --android`: Ordner, Papierkorb, Google Play). `device` overrides each slide's frame (no iPhone on Play); `slides` picks the seven that fit Android — not "album" (Android makes a folder).

//featureGraphic: Google Play feature graphic, exactly 1024x500 JPEG. slide: whose screen the phone shows; rawDir: the Android captures, like play-phone. Its copy is the featureGraphic block of every copy file (its subline shows with "subline": true). phone: width in percent of the height, tilt, nudge [x in widths, y in heights]. stickers: placed straight on the canvas — x in widths, y in heights, size in heights.
